description: Issues (Build.Rite): an issue logged against a VB page (with screenshots) is written up by the AI, analyzed against the page's code and the FDD (a verdict: fix on this page, fix elsewhere, works as designed, out of scope, needs information; for a fix, the exact change, checked), sent for approval (in the app, and an approval email from Microsoft 365), and once approved the agent applies it on a branch of its own (fix/<KEY>, the issue's number in the code's comments and the commit), tests it, pushes it and makes the pull request. Jira kept up to date. Like a software company's defect record: its details (type, severity, priority, environment, found in, fix version, customer and ticket, raised by and on, reporter email, assignee, due date), a discussion by anyone (comments, responses to the customer emailed to them, internal notes), verification in SIT/UAT, and a resolution with its root cause when closed. Its train is clickable (each step's own fields), a Next step bar says what to do; a table view shows every issue with its columns. desktop/lib/issues.js, /__issues/*, the desktop app.

info.description: { jira: { connected, project }, mail: { signedIn, account }, fix: { folder, branch, … } } or { ok: false, error }.

result.description: The last action's result: { ok, text }.

issue.description: The issue shown (with its fix: the analysis, the change, the tests).

edit.description: Its write-up being edited: { title, summary, steps (one per line), expected, actual, impact }.

pages.description: Every VB page, for the page picker: [{ id, label, appName, flow, page }].

images.description: Screenshots for the new issue: [{ name, mime, base64, url, w, h, size }].

layout.description: split (the list beside the issue) or table (every issue with its columns).

sortKey.description: The table's order: updated, severity, priority, raised, due.

stageView.description: The step of the train shown (0 Logged … 7 Closed); -1: the issue's own step.

det.description: The details being entered or changed: { kind, severity, priority, environment, foundIn, fixVersion, customer, customerRef, reportedBy, reporterEmail, raisedOn, assignee, dueDate }.

cKind.description: The discussion's next word: comment, response (to the customer) or internal (note).

cEmail.description: Email the response to the reporter.

approver.description: Who the approval email goes to (default: you).

vEnv.description: Verify: where the fix was tried.

rRes.description: Close: the resolution (fixed, done, as-designed, out-of-scope, moved, duplicate, cannot-reproduce, wont-fix).

rFixed.description: Close: the release it is fixed in.

project.description: The Jira project issues are created in.

pageSheet.description: The issue's page in Application pages: its technical sheet (facts, screenshots, AI text; saved, codeChanged) — shown in the Analyzed step.

cTo.description: An email's To (default: the Notify list and the reporter).

scope.description: The build in scope, from the top bar ('' for all; an app id): the list shows its issues, a new issue is logged in it.

agent.description: The agent's steps while it applies the change, and after (desktop/lib/issues.js progress): { running, done, okRun, error, seconds, steps: [{ key, label, state, detail, seconds }] }.

dApp.description: The new issue's build (an app id): chosen first; then one of its pages.

issueImages.description: The page module read screenshots pasted, dropped or attached in the new issue form (codeFixClient.queueImages).

focusRequest.description: Another screen handed this one an issue to open (shellBus.focus('issues', { id })).

scopeChanged.description: The build in scope was changed in the top bar (shellBus.onScope).
